name: Tessera Industries Blackout Carbine BC-4 'Lights Out'
description: A compact carbine that fires rounds containing Tessera's proprietary PhotoNull compound — a substance that absorbs and suppresses photonic activity within a 3-meter radius of the impact point for approximately 60 seconds. Within the affected zone, all light is absorbed: lamps go dark, screens black out, laser sights disappear, and human vision becomes useless. The compound works by releasing a dense aerosol of photon-absorbing nanoparticles that remain suspended in air, creating a sphere of absolute darkness. Thermal imaging is also degraded within the zone as the nanoparticles absorb infrared radiation. The weapon was designed for tactical entry operations where controlling the visual environment is paramount.
specifications:
caliber: 12mm PhotoNull compound round
magazine: 8 rounds
effective range: 20-80 meters
darkness radius: 3 meters from impact
darkness duration: 55-65 seconds
nanoparticle suspension: Aerosol, degrades naturally
thermal attenuation: approximately 70% within zone
weight: 3.1 kg
fire modes: Semi-automatic
story_hooks: An entire city block experienced 60 seconds of total darkness during which four people were killed — someone used multiple Blackout rounds to cover a coordinated assassination.
Tessera's PhotoNull compound has been loaded into building ventilation systems, creating zones of permanent darkness in occupied structures — someone is weaponizing architecture.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular carbine with a distinctly futuristic aesthetic. The silhouette is compact and purposeful, with a slightly tapered profile that narrows toward the muzzle. The weapon has a predatory, minimalist appearance—all function, no ornamentation. The receiver appears almost liquid in its curves, contrasting sharply with the rigid geometry of the barrel assembly.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 78 cm. Barrel length: 38 cm. Width across rails: 8 cm. Height with sight rail: 12 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and manageable at 3.1 kg despite its dense construction. The weight is distributed toward the receiver, making it feel stable and controlled rather than nose-heavy or unwieldy.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite frame with reinforced polymer sections. Internal mechanisms utilize precision-machined titanium alloy components. The barrel assembly features a specialized reactive metal housing designed to contain and channel the PhotoNull aerosol discharge.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte black with subtle graphite undertones. The surfaces appear almost non-reflective, designed to minimize tactical signatures. Wear patterns reveal burnished edges and micro-scratches from field use. Some Tessera units show residual photonic scorch marks—faint iridescent stains from compound detonation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: midnight black. Accents: deep navy blue striping along the rail systems and trigger guard. Minimal chrome detailing on the firing mechanism—only where necessary for durability.
physical_description.grip_texture: The forward grip is wrapped in non-slip polymer with a subtle honeycomb texture, designed for gloved operation. The pistol grip features aggressive knurling that feels almost sandpaper-rough—intentional for maintaining control during suppression operations. The charging handle is bare anodized aluminum, cool to the touch.
distinctive_features: Oversized muzzle brake with asymmetrical venting—allows aerosol cloud to expand in controlled pattern
Dual-stage ejection port with sealed chamber to contain compound residue
Integrated pressure-release valve on the gas tube, glowing faintly amber when charged
Rail-mounted photonic density indicator: a small digital readout showing nanoparticle suspension status
Custom serial placard with Tessera's theta-wave logo stamped in recessed lettering
Magazine well has a translucent polymer insert showing round count and compound integrity
Witness holes along the receiver for internal mechanism inspection
Subtle diagonal hatching on receiver sides to reduce glint
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries logo (concentric circles with theta symbol) stamped into the left-side receiver panel. 'BLACKOUT BC-4' engraved in clean sans-serif font along the barrel shroud. Hazmat notation—yellow and black striped diamond—appears on the magazine well and chamber door, indicating photon-suppression payload. Serial number marked in micro-etching on the lower receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained and regularly deployed. Most examples show minor scuffing on the muzzle brake and faint photonic scorching around the ejection port—evidence of compound detonation. Well-cared-for tactical weapons, kept clean but bearing the patina of operational use. Minimal wear on controls suggests disciplined operator base.
